stated: The Conservative Party will work with other countries to reform international asylum laws to make them fit for an age of mass migration, restricting visa access from countries that do not cooperate on national priorities like illegal migration.

source.quote: Reform asylum rules, holding an international summit and working with other countries to reform international laws to make them fit for an age of mass migration. We will restrict visa access from countries that don’t work with us on our national priorities, like illegal migration.

bearing_set.reason: The policy is explicitly framed around controlling illegal migration as a national-security/national-priority concern, directly engaging border security and the UK's resilience to cross-border threats — core O5 territory.

Reforming international asylum law alters the legal-rights framework governing asylum seekers' right to claim protection, due process in asylum determinations, and equal-treatment obligations under instruments such as the 1951 Refugee Convention and ECHR — all within O9's strict scope.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: a safety/security effect (O5) and a due-process/rule-of-law effect for asylum seekers (O9). Effects on prosperity (O13) or cohesion (O15) via migration-level changes are too indirect and mechanism-light to clear the non-negligible bar.
